narrative:
The model estimates a 68% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expected to stay.

Most influential was the number of training programs you attended during the last three years. At seven or more, this is higher than most employees who were predicted to stay (only 19% of them had this level). Surprisingly, the model sees this high participation as a signal that you may be preparing to move on, pushing the prediction toward leaving.

The second strongest factor is that you have received other job opportunities while working here. This is relatively uncommon—only 23% of employees predicted to stay reported receiving outside offers—yet it strongly increases the likelihood the model assigns to you eventually departing.

Your overall years of experience (more than 11 years) also contributed to the prediction of leaving. While many who stay have shorter careers, your extensive background appears to the model as giving you more external options, further tilting the outcome.

The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you, explore whether additional internal growth opportunities could increase your commitment, and consider whether the current role fully utilizes your experience. You may also want to reflect on whether the external opportunities align better with your long-term plans.
